decisions.statement: The unit of work is one check's audit rather than a whole audit run.
A turn is taken for each check rather than one turn for the service.
Two audits of one check never overlap.
Two audits of two checks may overlap.
A round runs several of its checks at one time rather than one after another.
How many run at one time is how many processors the round may use.
A round no group holds to a quota runs one check at a time.
A check is answered in the place that check was named rather than where it ended.
What turned red is read in that same order whichever check ended first.
A second asker inside one process waits on the first asker's answer.
A turn is waited on by a wait that holds the loop, so two in one process hang.
Askers share an answer only where check, home and commit all agree.
An asker whose check is clean at the asker's commit starts no run.
The verdict is read again once the turn is taken.
Many askers at one commit are answered by one run.
The commit a run answers for is read before the tree is walked.
The tree is walked once for a round rather than once for each check.
A round asks at the commit the round opened at, so every check in it runs.
Which checks a round runs is handed in rather than read off disk.
A round handed no check runs the checks its phase names.
A round handed checks runs those checks and no other.
A check handed in is run though no phase names that check.
A check handed in twice is run once.
A name that is no check's leaves a round the checks it does name.
A round opening while a round runs shares every check already underway.
A check that refused and a check that threw are told apart in the verdict.
A check that could not run is told as unmeasured rather than as refusing.
A check that both refused and could not run reads as unmeasured.
The round's exit line counts what refused apart from what nothing measured.
A telling that lands nowhere is said on the error stream and ends the round done.
The round's exit says whether the audit ran rather than whether a telling landed.
A verdict is written as each check is judged rather than once the round is over.
A verdict is read from the audit log beside the check's own page.
A verdict is sent to the pages service rather than into the tree the round holds.
What a check run apart cost is sent the same way a verdict is.
An asker may put a recorder of its own in place of the pages service.
A round waits for a verdict to land before answering the asker.
The process that judged a check writes that check's verdict.
A verdict is written here only where the log holds none at the commit asked.
A carried verdict is written here, no process having run to write it.
A check is audited in a process of its own rather than in the round's process.
The memory that process held goes back to the machine as that process ends.
What the check judged comes back through a file rather than the output stream.
The processor ceiling that check's audit group states is put on that process.
A check sharing a machine with the checks beside it spends more than it would alone.
A check refusing over its own page is run again alone before the round keeps that refusal.
A refusal naming the check's own page is about the run rather than about the tree.
Every other refusal names a path in the tree, which a second run would not move.
The ceiling is read against that second run rather than against the first.
The second run is taken once the round's lanes are drained, so it runs alone.
A round with no check refusing over its own page runs nothing a second time.
A check run again takes the turn its own slug names, as the first run did.
The verdict the second run leaves is written over the one the shared run left.
A check turning clean alone is told to nobody.
A check refusing alone as well is run no third time.
A check that runs away is stopped there rather than holding the round open.
The memory ceiling that group states is put on that process where one is stated.
A group stating no ceiling leaves that process held to none.
A process ended by a signal reads as a check that could not run.
A check killed at its own processor ceiling and one killed from outside die on one signal.
A check a signal ended is run again alone, its refusal naming its own page.
The round after is what runs an unmeasured check again, no verdict carrying it.
A process exiting other than zero reads as a check that could not run.
The refusal for either carries what that process said on its error stream.
A file that is absent or says no verdict reads as a check that could not run.
A spawn that throws reads as a check that could not run, and the round goes on.
The refusal for any of those names the check's own page.
The file the verdict comes back through is swept whether the check ran or not.
A process that answered records what its own run cost.
A process that died records nothing, so what that run cost is recorded here.
The seconds recorded are the ones the ceiling was measured against.
A run whose environment names no home is refused before any check runs.
Nothing here asks for an audit on another agent's behalf.
A round telling by refusal has been watched on the service that runs it.
A check whose input never moved since its verdict is carried rather than run.
A carried verdict keeps the moment it ran and takes the newer commit.
The files moved between two commits are asked of git.
A span is asked of git once however many checks ask for that span.
A check naming no input is run rather than carried.
A span git could not answer is run rather than carried.
An asker handing over no span carries nothing forward.
A verdict that refused is carried forward as a verdict that refuses.
A check's audit waits for the memory a landing starts on before its process opens.

definition: one check's audit run under a turn of its own, and the round running them all
